question_text: What is semantic HTML, and why do elements like main, nav, and article matter beyond styling?
reference_answer: Semantic elements convey structural meaning to screen readers, keyboard navigation tools, and search crawlers rather than presenting anonymous div wrappers, improving accessibility and SEO automatically.

question_text: Explain the difference between block, inline, and inline-block CSS display values.
reference_answer: Block elements start on a new line taking full available width; inline elements flow horizontally within text ignoring width/height; inline-block flows inline while respecting explicit width, height, and vertical margins.

question_text: Describe the four layers of the CSS Box Model and what box-sizing: border-box changes.
reference_answer: From inside out: content, padding, border, and margin. Standard content-box adds padding and border on top of width, whereas border-box includes padding and border inside the declared width/height.

question_text: Compare CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid and when to choose each.
reference_answer: Flexbox arranges items along one primary axis (row or column) ideal for navbars and toolbars; CSS Grid coordinates two dimensions (rows and columns simultaneously) ideal for full page layouts and card matrices.

question_text: What is CSS specificity, and how are selector weights ordered?
reference_answer: Specificity resolves conflicting CSS rules by scoring selector types: inline styles > IDs (#id) > classes/attributes/pseudo-classes (.cls) > elements/pseudo-elements (div), with !important overriding unless matched at higher specificity.

question_text: Compare var, let, and const in JavaScript regarding scope, hoisting, and reassignment.
reference_answer: var is function-scoped and hoisted initialized as undefined; let and const are block-scoped in the Temporal Dead Zone until declaration, with const preventing variable reassignment (though object properties remain mutable).

question_text: Explain the difference between == and === in JavaScript.
reference_answer: == performs loose comparison with implicit type coercion (e.g., 0 == '0' is true), whereas === checks strict equality matching both value and data type without coercion.

question_text: What is a closure in JavaScript, and give a practical use case.
reference_answer: A closure is a function bundled with references to its surrounding lexical environment, letting inner functions remember private outer variables after the outer function returns—used for counters, memoization, and event handlers.

question_text: Explain what the DOM (Document Object Model) is and how the browser renders a webpage from HTML and CSS.
reference_answer: The browser parses HTML into the DOM tree and CSS into the CSSOM tree, merges them into a Render Tree, computes Layout box geometry, and Paints/Composites layers onto the screen.

question_text: What is event bubbling in the DOM, and how do stopPropagation() and preventDefault() differ?
reference_answer: Event bubbling sends triggered child events upward through parent ancestors to document; stopPropagation() halts that upward traversal, whereas preventDefault() cancels native browser actions like form submit reload.

question_text: Explain JavaScript Promises and compare .then() chaining with async/await.
reference_answer: A Promise represents an eventual async outcome (pending, fulfilled, or rejected); async/await provides syntactic sugar over Promise chains allowing readable linear try/catch error handling without deeply nested callbacks.

question_text: Compare the primary HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
reference_answer: GET retrieves resources without side effects; POST creates resources or triggers actions; PUT replaces an entire resource idempotently; PATCH partially updates fields; DELETE removes a resource.

question_text: Explain common HTTP status code ranges (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx) with concrete examples.
reference_answer: 2xx signals success (200 OK, 201 Created); 3xx handles redirects (301, 304 Not Modified); 4xx denotes client errors (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found); 5xx indicates server failures (500, 502, 503).

question_text: What is the difference between HTTP 401 Unauthorized and HTTP 403 Forbidden?
reference_answer: 401 means the client lacks valid authentication credentials (who are you?); 403 means the client is authenticated successfully, yet lacks permission/role rights to access that specific resource.

question_text: What is CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing), and why do browsers enforce it?
reference_answer: CORS controls whether a web page at origin A (scheme+host+port) may read responses from API origin B via server-returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, protecting users' authenticated sessions from rogue sites.

question_text: Compare localStorage, sessionStorage, and HTTP cookies for client-side storage.
reference_answer: localStorage persists ~5-10MB per origin across browser restarts; sessionStorage clears when the tab closes; cookies hold tiny (~4KB) payloads automatically sent with matching HTTP requests and support HttpOnly security flags.

question_text: What is a JSON Web Token (JWT), and what are its three dot-separated segments?
reference_answer: A JWT is a signed stateless token composed of base64url-encoded Header (algorithm/type), Payload (claims like sub and exp), and cryptographic Signature verifying integrity without server-side session lookup.

question_text: Why should JWTs never store sensitive secrets like passwords in their payload?
reference_answer: JWT payloads are merely Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted, meaning anyone holding the token can decode and inspect every claim directly in plaintext.

question_text: What is SQL Injection (SQLi), and what is the primary defense against it?
reference_answer: SQLi injects malicious SQL syntax through unsanitized user inputs concatenated into query strings; using parameterized queries / prepared statements keeps code structure strictly separate from user data values.

question_text: What is Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and how do you defend against it in modern web apps?
reference_answer: XSS injects executable JavaScript into trusted pages rendered to victims; defenses include context-aware HTML output escaping, avoiding unsafe innerHTML sinks, Content Security Policy (CSP), and HttpOnly session cookies.

question_text: Explain Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) at a high level.
reference_answer: CSRF tricks a logged-in victim's browser into sending unintended state-changing requests (automatically carrying session cookies) from a malicious third-party page; SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens block it.

question_text: What does HTTPS add over plain HTTP?
reference_answer: HTTPS wraps HTTP inside TLS encryption, guaranteeing confidentiality against eavesdropping, data integrity against tampering in transit, and server identity verification via X.509 certificates.

question_text: What is REST, and what makes an API RESTful?
reference_answer: REST models application data as URI-identified resources manipulated uniformly via stateless standard HTTP verbs, clean representations (JSON), and appropriate status codes without server-held client session state.

question_text: Explain debouncing vs throttling in frontend JavaScript performance optimization.
reference_answer: Debouncing waits until an event stops firing for X ms before running once (e.g., search autocomplete), whereas throttling limits execution to at most once every X ms during continuous bursts (e.g., scroll tracking).

question_text: What are path parameters, query parameters, and request body payloads in HTTP APIs?
reference_answer: Path params identify a specific resource (/users/42), query params filter/sort/paginate (?topic=python&page=2), and request bodies carry structured creation/update data safely in POST/PUT/PATCH calls.

question_text: What is Pydantic doing in a FastAPI backend endpoint?
reference_answer: Pydantic validates incoming JSON types, constraints, and defaults at runtime using Python type annotations, automatically returning structured HTTP 422 errors on invalid input and generating OpenAPI schemas.

question_text: Explain responsive web design and CSS media queries.
reference_answer: Responsive design adapts layouts fluidly across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports using relative units (rem, %, vw), flexible grids, and @media breakpoints targeting viewport widths or capabilities.

question_text: What is ARIA in web accessibility, and what is the first rule of ARIA?
reference_answer: ARIA attributes communicate dynamic roles, states (aria-expanded), and live regions to assistive tech; the first rule of ARIA is to prefer native HTML elements (button, input) before adding ARIA attributes.

question_text: Explain why passwords must be hashed with slow salted algorithms (bcrypt/Argon2) rather than SHA-256.
reference_answer: Fast hashes like SHA-256 allow billions of brute-force guesses per second on GPUs; per-user salted bcrypt or Argon2id enforces intentional memory/CPU work factors thwarting rainbow tables and cracking.

question_text: What is the purpose of an HTTP ETag header?
reference_answer: An ETag versions a response representation so clients can send If-None-Match on subsequent requests, allowing the server to reply cheaply with 304 Not Modified when content hasn't changed.

question_text: Contrast Server-Side Rendering (SSR) vs Client-Side Rendering (CSR).
reference_answer: SSR renders complete HTML per request on the server for fast First Contentful Paint and SEO, whereas CSR ships a minimal HTML shell and builds UI dynamically via JavaScript in the browser.

question_text: What is an environment variable (.env), and why must API keys never be bundled into frontend code?
reference_answer: Environment variables configure secrets per deployment environment outside source control; any key placed in frontend JS/HTML is shipped to every user's browser DevTools and can be stolen instantly.

question_text: Explain the difference between async and defer attributes on an HTML script tag.
reference_answer: Normal scripts block HTML parsing immediately; async downloads in parallel and executes right when ready (out of order); defer downloads in parallel and runs sequentially only after HTML parsing completes.

question_text: What is the difference between undefined and null in JavaScript?
reference_answer: undefined means a variable has been declared or an argument/property omitted without any assigned value; null is an explicit intentional assignment indicating an empty object value.

question_text: Explain higher-order array methods map(), filter(), and reduce() in JavaScript.
reference_answer: map() transforms each item into a new same-length array; filter() keeps elements passing a predicate; reduce() folds an array left-to-right into a single accumulated value without mutating the source array.

question_text: What is DNS resolution when a user enters a URL into the browser?
reference_answer: DNS translates a human-readable domain name (example.com) through browser/OS caches, recursive resolver, root, TLD, and authoritative nameservers into the server's routable IP address.

question_text: What is pagination in REST APIs, and compare page/limit vs cursor pagination?
reference_answer: Pagination splits large result sets into chunks; page/offset is simple for random page jumps while slowing on deep offsets, whereas cursor pagination stays fast O(1) and avoids skipped/duplicate items under live inserts.

question_text: What is Dependency Injection in FastAPI routes using Depends()?
reference_answer: Depends() declares reusable per-request dependencies (like DB sessions or current authenticated user checks) that FastAPI resolves, injects automatically into endpoints, caches per request, and simplifies test mocking.

question_text: What is Gzip or Brotli compression in HTTP responses?
reference_answer: When a browser sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, br, servers compress JSON/HTML/CSS payloads before transmission and mark Content-Encoding, shrinking bandwidth by 60-80% cleanly.

question_text: Explain the difference between WebSockets and standard HTTP polling for live updates.
reference_answer: HTTP polling repeatedly opens requests asking for changes; WebSockets upgrade once to a persistent full-duplex TCP connection enabling instant bidirectional server push with low overhead.

question_text: What is an API Gateway or Reverse Proxy (like Nginx) doing in front of a backend web app?
reference_answer: It terminates TLS, serves static assets, routes paths, enforces rate limits, adds compression/security headers, and load-balances traffic safely across internal application workers.

question_text: What is semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for APIs and packages?
reference_answer: MAJOR increments indicate breaking incompatible changes; MINOR adds backward-compatible functionality; PATCH delivers backward-compatible bug fixes or security updates.

question_text: Explain why Streamlit reruns the Python script top-to-bottom on widget interactions and what st.session_state solves.
reference_answer: Every button click triggers a clean script rerun; local Python variables reset on each pass, whereas st.session_state persists per-user values, auth tokens, and active interview timers safely across reruns.

question_text: What is MIME type (Content-Type header), and why does X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff matter?
reference_answer: Content-Type tells clients how to interpret bytes (e.g., application/json vs text/html); nosniff disables browser MIME-sniffing heuristics so uploaded text files cannot accidentally be executed as JavaScript or HTML.

question_text: Explain the difference between Authentication and Authorization with a web endpoint example.
reference_answer: Authentication verifies identity (validating an OTP or password login to issue a session); Authorization checks privileges (verifying an admin role before permitting POST /api/v1/scraping/run).

question_text: Walk through the JavaScript Event Loop, Call Stack, Web APIs, Macrotask Queue, and Microtask Queue execution order.
reference_answer: Synchronous call-stack frames finish completely first; next the Event Loop drains the entire Microtask Queue (Promise callbacks, queueMicrotask) before executing one Macrotask (setTimeout, I/O), repeating after optional render frames.

question_text: What triggers a CORS preflight OPTIONS request, and how do servers optimize preflight latency?
reference_answer: Non-simple requests (PUT/DELETE, application/json bodies, custom Authorization headers) trigger an automatic OPTIONS preflight; returning Access-Control-Max-Age caches preflight approval in the browser for hours.

question_text: Compare Cookie-based Server Sessions vs Stateless JWT authentication regarding revocation, XSS, CSRF, and scaling.
reference_answer: Server sessions in Redis allow instant revocation and tiny opaque cookie IDs, protected against XSS via HttpOnly; JWTs avoid DB lookup on read horizontally, yet instant revocation requires short TTLs + refresh-token rotation + denylist.

question_text: How does OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE protect public SPAs and mobile apps?
reference_answer: Without a confidential client secret, SPAs generate a random code_verifier and send its SHA-256 code_challenge; only the app holding the original code_verifier can later swap the authorization code for tokens, thwarting code interception.

question_text: Explain how SameSite cookie attributes (Strict, Lax, None) protect against CSRF attacks.
reference_answer: Strict withholds cookies on all cross-site requests; Lax allows top-level safe GET navigation links while blocking cross-site POSTs/embeds; None permits cross-site cookies only when paired with HTTPS Secure flag.

question_text: Compare sync def vs async def path operations in FastAPI and explain what blocks the event loop.
reference_answer: FastAPI runs async def directly on Uvicorn's asyncio event loop (ideal for async network I/O) and dispatches regular def routes to AnyIO worker threads; running synchronous CPU/DB calls inside async def freezes every concurrent request.

question_text: How does Event Delegation improve performance and dynamic UI handling in vanilla DOM programming?
reference_answer: Instead of attaching hundreds of listeners to list items individually, one listener on a common parent inspects event.target.closest() via bubbling—slashing memory overhead and working seamlessly on dynamically added nodes.

question_text: Explain HTTP idempotency and why POST creates duplicates on retry unless an Idempotency-Key header is enforced.
reference_answer: GET, PUT, and DELETE leave identical resource state when retried, whereas POST creates new records each call; storing an Idempotency-Key hash alongside the cached result in Redis/DB makes retried payment or booking POSTs safe.

question_text: Compare GraphQL and REST across over-fetching, caching, N+1 queries, and schema evolution.
reference_answer: GraphQL eliminates over/under-fetching via strongly typed client queries and clean versionless evolution, yet breaks standard HTTP URL/CDN caching and introduces DataLoader-needing N+1 resolver hazards unless batched.

question_text: Compare WebSockets, Server-Sent Events (SSE), and Long Polling for streaming LLM tokens or live alerts.
reference_answer: SSE streams UTF-8 server-to-client events cleanly over standard HTTP/2 with automatic browser reconnects—ideal for LLM token streaming; WebSockets fit true bidirectional real-time apps like collaborative editors or audio streaming.

question_text: Explain Content Security Policy (CSP) directives and how nonces eliminate inline script XSS risks.
reference_answer: CSP headers restrict allowed origins for scripts, styles, and frames (default-src 'self'). Using per-response cryptographic nonces on script tags with strict-dynamic permits legitimate scripts while blocking attacker-injected inline JS.

question_text: Explain Critical Rendering Path bottlenecks (render-blocking CSS, layout thrashing, reflows vs repaints).
reference_answer: Render-blocking CSS delays First Paint; interleaving DOM style reads (offsetWidth) followed by writes inside loops forces synchronous Layout Thrashing (reflows), whereas GPU-composited transforms/opacity animate cleanly skipping layout and paint.

question_text: Compare Promise.all, Promise.allSettled, Promise.race, and Promise.any in JavaScript.
reference_answer: Promise.all fast-fails on the first rejection; Promise.allSettled waits for all outcomes returning status/value/reason; Promise.race settles with the very first resolved or rejected promise; Promise.any resolves on the first fulfillment.

question_text: Explain JavaScript prototypal inheritance and how ES6 class syntax maps onto prototypes.
reference_answer: Objects delegate missing property lookups along an internal [[Prototype]] chain up to Object.prototype; ES6 classes are syntactic sugar placing methods cleanly on Constructor.prototype while wiring extends via Object.setPrototypeOf.

question_text: What does 'this' bind to across regular functions, arrow functions, methods, call/apply/bind, and strict mode?
reference_answer: Regular calls bind global/undefined (strict mode); method calls bind the receiver left of the dot; new binds the created instance; call/apply/bind set explicitly; arrow functions inherit 'this' lexically from enclosing scope forever.

question_text: Explain Cache-Control directives: public, private, max-age, s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate, and no-store.
reference_answer: no-store disables all caching (banking/secrets); private restricts caching to the user's browser; public allows CDNs using s-maxage; stale-while-revalidate serves slightly expired content immediately while refreshing asynchronously in the background.

question_text: Compare HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 (QUIC) regarding head-of-line blocking and multiplexing.
reference_answer: HTTP/1.1 opens multiple connections suffering application HOL blocking; HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over one TCP connection (still vulnerable to TCP packet-loss HOL blocking); HTTP/3 runs over UDP QUIC eliminating cross-stream transport HOL blocking and speeding handshakes.

question_text: How do you implement secure Email OTP authentication against brute-force guessing, replay, and timing side-channels?
reference_answer: Store only a salted/HMAC-hashed OTP with short TTL (5-10 min), enforce atomic verification attempt counters locking after 3-5 tries, invalidate single-use codes immediately inside a DB transaction, rate-limit sends, and use constant-time hmac.compare_digest.

question_text: Why can SQLite throw 'database is locked' in a multi-worker FastAPI app, and how do WAL mode and busy_timeout mitigate it?
reference_answer: Default rollback journals block readers during writes; enabling PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL allows concurrent readers alongside one writer, while busy_timeout waits cleanly on brief write locks alongside short focused transactions.

question_text: Compare Streamlit fragments (@st.fragment), @st.cache_data, and @st.cache_resource.
reference_answer: @st.cache_data serializes and caches pure computation results like DataFrames/API lists; @st.cache_resource shares singletons like ML models or DB pools across reruns; @st.fragment reruns only an isolated UI block locally without redrawing the whole page.

question_text: Explain how Refresh Token Rotation with reuse detection strengthens JWT web sessions.
reference_answer: Access tokens stay short-lived (5-15m); every refresh endpoint call invalidates the old single-use refresh token and issues a new pair. If a stolen older refresh token is ever replayed, the entire token family is revoked immediately.

question_text: What is Open Redirect vulnerability, and how should post-login redirect URLs be validated safely?
reference_answer: Blindly redirecting to ?next=https://evil.com enables convincing phishing attacks off trusted domains; validate redirects strictly as relative paths starting with single '/' (not '//') or match against an exact domain allowlist.

question_text: Explain FastAPI Middleware vs Dependency Injection: when is each the right abstraction?
reference_answer: ASGI Middleware wraps every request/response globally for logging, request-ID tracing, GZip, or CORS headers; Dependencies execute per-router/route cleanly with OpenAPI documentation for auth verification, RBAC roles, and DB transactions.

question_text: How do Web Workers prevent heavy JavaScript calculations from freezing UI animations and input?
reference_answer: Web Workers spawn separate OS background threads lacking direct DOM access, processing heavy parsing or crypto work asynchronously and exchanging structured cloned messages cleanly with the main UI thread.

question_text: Compare optimistic UI updates with pessimistic UI updates and rollback patterns.
reference_answer: Pessimistic UI disables controls showing a spinner until the server confirms success; Optimistic UI updates local state immediately (like bookmark toggles) and rolls back cleanly with an error toast if the async API request fails.

question_text: Explain CSRF prevention patterns when a React/SPA frontend calls a separate REST backend.
reference_answer: Either store short-lived tokens securely and transmit via Authorization: Bearer headers (immune to automatic cookie CSRF) or set HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookies paired with a Double-Submit / Synchronizer CSRF header checked server-side.

question_text: Explain Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in URL-fetching or webhook backends and how to prevent it.
reference_answer: SSRF tricks the backend into requesting internal cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) or private VPC ports via user-supplied URLs; mitigate by resolving DNS first, blocking RFC1918/link-local IPs before dialing, disabling redirects, and allowlisting hosts.

question_text: How do BackgroundTasks in FastAPI differ from dedicated distributed task queues like Celery or ARQ?
reference_answer: FastAPI BackgroundTasks run in-process inside the worker right after returning the response—fine for lightweight email sends, yet lost on crash/restart and competing for worker CPU; Celery/ARQ persist retries cleanly in Redis/RabbitMQ workers.

question_text: Explain Tree Shaking and Code Splitting in modern frontend bundlers (Vite / Webpack).
reference_answer: Tree shaking statically analyzes ES Module imports/exports to strip dead unused library code; Code splitting chunks routes and heavy modals dynamically via import() so users download only code needed for the initial screen.

question_text: What are Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), and what concrete mistakes hurt each metric?
reference_answer: LCP measures main content paint speed (hurt by unoptimized hero images/SSR delay); INP measures interaction-to-next-paint latency (hurt by long main-thread JS tasks); CLS measures unexpected layout shifts (hurt by unsized images and late banners).

question_text: Compare Hydration, Streaming SSR, and React Server Components (RSC) in modern full-stack frameworks.
reference_answer: Traditional SSR hydrates the whole JS bundle on the client before interactivity; Streaming SSR flushes HTML chunks progressively as async DB calls resolve; RSC runs server-only components permanently on the server keeping zero bundle weight on clients.

question_text: How do you validate multipart file uploads securely on a backend API (PDF/resume/audio)?
reference_answer: Enforce strict max byte limits during chunked streaming, verify magic-byte file headers rather than trusting file extensions/Content-Type alone, store outside web-executable directories with randomized UUID names, and scan/sandbox parsers.

question_text: Explain CSS Containment and Virtualized Lists (Windowing) for rendering 10,000+ rows smoothly.
reference_answer: Rendering 10,000 DOM nodes bloats layout and memory; Virtualization mounts only the ~20 rows visible inside the viewport plus a tiny overscan buffer while updating transforms on scroll, maintaining 60fps.

question_text: Compare Structured Logging, Correlation/Request IDs, and Health/Readiness probes (/health vs /ready) in backend APIs.
reference_answer: Correlation IDs attach a trace UUID across logs and downstream calls for rapid incident debugging; /health checks whether the process is alive while /ready verifies DB pools and external dependencies can accept traffic cleanly.

question_text: Explain Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy pitfalls in JavaScript (Object.assign / spread vs structuredClone).
reference_answer: Spread syntax ({...obj}) only clones top-level keys, sharing nested object references secretly; structuredClone() deep-clones nested structures, Maps, Sets, and Dates natively without JSON.stringify's Date/undefined data loss.

question_text: What is Exponential Backoff with Jitter in resilient API clients, and why is jitter essential?
reference_answer: Retrying after base * 2^attempt prevents hammering struggling backends; adding randomized full jitter breaks synchronized retry thundering herds when thousands of clients fail at the same millisecond.

question_text: Compare Content Negotiation (Accept header) and API Versioning strategies (URI /v1/ vs Header vs Query).
reference_answer: URI versioning (/api/v1/questions) is explicit, debuggable, and CDN-cache friendly at the cost of route duplication; Header versioning keeps clean canonical URLs though harder to inspect directly in browser bars.

question_text: How does the Browser Same-Origin Policy apply differently to HTML img/script embeds vs fetch()/XHR requests?
reference_answer: HTML embeds (images, scripts, styles) load cross-origin resources fairly freely without reading raw pixels/source, whereas JS programmatic fetch()/XHR reads are strictly blocked by SOP unless the target explicitly grants CORS headers.

question_text: Explain TypeScript Structural Typing, Discriminated Unions, and why 'unknown' is safer than 'any'.
reference_answer: any disables type checking entirely; unknown forces explicit type narrowing before use; Discriminated Unions share a literal tag field (kind: 'ok' | 'err') enabling exhaustive compile-time switch safety.

question_text: Explain Memory Leaks in single-page JavaScript apps and how DevTools Heap Snapshots reveal them.
reference_answer: Forgotten window event listeners, uncleared setInterval timers, detached DOM node references held in closures, and unbounded caches prevent garbage collection; comparing retained paths across two Heap Snapshots exposes surviving leaks.

question_text: Compare Pydantic v2 validation speed, model_validator, and response_model filtering in FastAPI.
reference_answer: Pydantic v2's Rust-backed core runs 5-20x faster than v1; specifying response_model automatically strips sensitive internal fields like password_hash before serializing responses even if DB objects carry extra columns.

question_text: How do TLS 1.3 1-RTT handshakes and OCSP Stapling reduce HTTPS connection setup latency?
reference_answer: TLS 1.3 merges key exchange directly into the client's first ClientHello saving a round-trip over TLS 1.2 (plus optional 0-RTT resumption), while OCSP Stapling embeds cached certificate revocation proof inside the handshake sparing clients external lookups.

question_text: Explain Graceful Shutdown in Uvicorn/FastAPI servers during rolling deployments.
reference_answer: On SIGTERM, load balancers stop sending new traffic while the ASGI server stops accepting new sockets, drains active HTTP/WebSocket requests within a grace timeout, executes lifespan shutdown hooks closing DB pools, and exits cleanly.

question_text: How do you protect an OTP / Login backend endpoint behind Nginx or Cloudflare from IP-spoofing rate-limit bypasses?
reference_answer: Attackers spoof X-Forwarded-For headers trivially; configure the app/limiter to trust forwarded headers strictly from known local reverse-proxy CIDRs while taking the rightmost untrusted hop added by the edge proxy.

question_text: Explain CSS Stacking Contexts and why z-index: 9999 sometimes fails to appear above another element.
reference_answer: Properties like opacity < 1, transform, filter, or isolation: isolate create isolated local Stacking Contexts; a child with z-index: 9999 cannot escape above a sibling of its parent stacking context that sits higher.

question_text: Diagnose why a FastAPI endpoint stays slow under 200 concurrent requests even though individual PostgreSQL queries take only 3ms.
reference_answer: Check whether async endpoints accidentally call sync blocking drivers (like synchronous requests, boto3, or psycopg2 blocking the single asyncio loop), whether the DB connection pool max_size is starved queueing requests, or if CPU-heavy JSON/PDF parsing saturates Python's GIL without worker processes.

question_text: Design a secure, abuse-resistant Email OTP & JWT authentication subsystem supporting multi-device login and instant session revocation.
reference_answer: Hash 6-digit OTPs with per-token HMAC-SHA256 + 5-min TTL + atomic 5-attempt lockout + dual IP & per-email sliding-window rate limits (returning uniform generic responses against enumeration). Issue 10-min stateless RS256 access JWTs paired with opaque HttpOnly SameSite=Lax rotated refresh tokens tracked in DB/Redis with family-reuse revocation and per-device logout.

question_text: How do WebSocket scaling architectures handle pub/sub fanout across 10 stateless backend container replicas behind an L7 load balancer?
reference_answer: Because TCP WebSocket state lives pinned in one container's RAM, replicas subscribe to a shared Redis Pub/Sub or NATS backplane keyed by room/session ID; incoming messages publish to the broker so whichever replica owns a recipient's socket flushes frames smoothly, backed by sticky heartbeats and reconnect cursors.

question_text: Compare Micro-frontends vs Monorepo SPAs: analyze bundle bloat, shared state coupling, CSS leakage, and deployment trade-offs.
reference_answer: Micro-frontends enable independent team releases via Module Federation or edge composition, yet multiply shared framework duplicates unless strictly aligned, risk cross-team UX/routing version skew, and demand Shadow DOM or CSS Modules scoping; modular monorepos with strict package boundaries usually scale cleanly for smaller orgs.

question_text: Explain Browser Origin Isolation, Spectre mitigations (COOP / COEP / CORP), and why SharedArrayBuffer requires Cross-Origin Isolation.
reference_answer: Spectre side-channels allow shared process JS timers to read secret memory across origins; Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (same-origin) + Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (require-corp) force dedicated OS process isolation so high-resolution SharedArrayBuffer audio/WASM DSP threads run safely.

question_text: Design a resilient real-time Audio Interview streaming frontend + backend pipeline (mic capture -> ASR -> LLM -> audio/text feedback) over unstable networks.
reference_answer: Browser captures opus/PCM chunks via AudioWorklet with VAD silence detection and client sequence IDs; chunked uploads or WebSocket stream to backend maintaining idempotent turn IDs so temporary drops reconnect seamlessly without duplicate scoring; backend streams LLM feedback progressively over SSE while keeping heavy transcription off the async event loop.

question_text: Analyze the subtle security flaws in naive JWT implementations (alg: none, HS256/RS256 key confusion, weak secrets, missing iss/aud checks).
reference_answer: Accepting alg: none skips signature checks; RS256-to-HS256 confusion tricks libraries into verifying HMAC using a known public PEM key as the HMAC secret. Always hardcode expected allowed asymmetric algorithms (algorithms=['RS256']), validate iss/aud/exp claims strictly, rotate signing keys via JWKS kid headers, and avoid dynamic key lookup from untrusted headers.

question_text: How does React Fiber (concurrent reconciliation) avoid blocking user input on massive component re-renders compared to legacy stack reconciliation?
reference_answer: Legacy stack recursion walked the whole virtual DOM synchronously freezing frames; React Fiber structures work as a linked-list tree broken into small interruptible units scheduled across frames, yielding between slices for high-priority user inputs (useTransition/urgent lanes) before committing DOM mutations atomically.

question_text: Explain Cache Stampede (Dogpiling) in web APIs backed by Redis/CDN and compare Mutex locking vs Probabilistic Early Expiration (XFetch).
reference_answer: When a hot cached key expires simultaneously under heavy traffic, thousands of workers miss together and crush the origin DB; request coalescing (singleflight mutex per cache key) lets one worker recompute while others wait, whereas XFetch recomputes probabilistically just before TTL expiry using compute-time weighting with zero lock contention.

question_text: Walk through debugging an intermittent 502 Bad Gateway between Nginx reverse proxy and a Python Gunicorn/Uvicorn upstream under load.
reference_answer: Typical causes include Keep-Alive race conditions (upstream idle_timeout shorter than Nginx proxy keepalive causing Nginx to reuse a freshly closed socket -> tune backend keepalive > proxy timeout), sync worker exhaustion/OOM kills on burst payloads, mismatched proxy_read_timeout on slow LLM endpoints, or exhausted ephemeral listen backlog (somaxconn).

question_text: Compare SQLite-backed Streamlit deployments vs multi-worker FastAPI + PostgreSQL when scaling from prototype to multi-tenant production.
reference_answer: Streamlit executes single-session stateful WebSocket scripts sharing OS memory cleanly for prototypes, yet global Python reruns and SQLite single-writer locks bottle high concurrency; isolating FastAPI stateless async workers backed by PostgreSQL connection pools (PgBouncer) + Redis locks + decoupled CDN static frontend handles thousands of concurrent users cleanly.

question_text: Explain DOM XSS via third-party Markdown/HTML rendering and design a defense-in-depth sanitizer pipeline.
reference_answer: User or LLM-generated HTML containing inline event handlers (onerror/onload) or javascript: links executes scripts when injected raw; defense-in-depth escapes HTML unconditionally at DB storage, renders strictly safe Markdown AST (no raw HTML passthrough), applies allowlist sanitization (DOMPurify / bleach) stripping event attributes/URL schemes, and enforces strict CSP script-src.

question_text: How do HTTP/2 Server Push deprecation and 103 Early Hints compare for speeding up page loads?
reference_answer: HTTP/2 Push often wasted bandwidth pushing assets already in browser cache and fought cross-tab prioritization; HTTP 103 Early Hints lets the server send lightweight Link: preload headers immediately while the backend still computes database SSR work, letting the browser warm CSS/fonts cleanly only if uncached.

question_text: Design an end-to-end Zero-Downtime Database Schema Migration strategy for a live 24/7 web backend without dropping requests.
reference_answer: Apply the Expand-Migrate-Contract pattern: (1) Expand by adding new nullable columns/tables and deploying dual-write backend code supporting both schemas cleanly; (2) Backfill historical rows in throttled batches; (3) Switch reads to the new schema and verify; (4) Deploy final cleanup removing legacy read/write paths before dropping old columns safely.

question_text: Analyze Subresource Integrity (SRI), Trusted Types API, and Permissions-Policy headers in hardening high-security web apps.
reference_answer: SRI checks cryptographic hashes on external CDN scripts preventing supply-chain tampering; Trusted Types blocks raw string injection into dangerous DOM sinks (innerHTML, eval) requiring audited sanitization policies; Permissions-Policy disables unwanted camera/mic/geolocation APIs across embedded frames.

question_text: How do browsers prioritize network requests, and how can resource hints (preload, preconnect, prefetch, fetchpriority) backfire if overused?
reference_answer: Browsers assign high priority to blocking CSS/scripts and lower priority to late images/async fetches; marking too many elements preload or fetchpriority='high' saturates the early TCP/HTTP2 window delaying critical LCP CSS/hero paint, while unconsumed preloads waste mobile data triggering console warnings.

question_text: Explain Distributed Tracing (OpenTelemetry traceparent W3C header) connecting a browser SPA, FastAPI gateway, and downstream ML microservices.
reference_answer: The frontend or edge proxy injects a W3C traceparent (trace-id, parent-span-id) propagating cleanly across async HTTP/gRPC/queue headers; each service attaches child spans capturing DB query timings, cache misses, and LLM token latency so waterfall flamegraphs pinpoint bottlenecks across every tier.

question_text: Diagnose subtle bugs caused by async race conditions in React/SPA data fetching when users type quickly or switch tabs, and how to solve them.
reference_answer: Earlier slower requests can resolve AFTER newer requests and overwrite fresh UI state (out-of-order response clobbering); mitigate by attaching an AbortController signal per effect cleanup to cancel stale fetches and guarding state updates with request sequence checks or TanStack Query cache keys.

question_text: Compare BFF (Backend for Frontend) architecture vs exposing raw internal microservices directly to web/mobile clients.
reference_answer: Direct microservice calls trigger chatty client waterfalls, leak internal service boundaries, and duplicate token/CORS logic across clients; a dedicated BFF per client type terminates auth cookies securely via OAuth tokens server-side, aggregates parallel downstream payloads, and tailors minimal schemas cleanly.

question_text: How do you guarantee transactional consistency between updating PostgreSQL user state and publishing an outbox email/webhook event?
reference_answer: Writing to DB then calling an external SMTP/Kafka broker risks partial failure (DB commits yet email drops, or vice versa); apply the Transactional Outbox pattern inserting the event row in the exact same ACID DB transaction, then relay reliably with idempotent workers.

question_text: Explain CORS-safelisted pitfalls with Credentials: include and Wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * in credentialed APIs.
reference_answer: Browsers reject Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * whenever Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true is set; servers mistakenly reflecting arbitrary Origin headers back dynamically break security completely unless matched strictly against an explicit exact-origin allowlist plus Vary: Origin for caches.

question_text: Analyze how Event Loop Starvation occurs in Node.js or Python asyncio APIs under adversarial JSON/Regex inputs (ReDoS).
reference_answer: Catastrophic backtracking regular expressions or deeply nested massive JSON payloads lock the single JS/asyncio thread cleanly for seconds on 1 CPU core, halting all health checks and concurrent users; enforce payload byte/depth limits, use linear-time RE2/non-backtracking patterns, and run untrusted heavy parsing in bounded worker pools.

question_text: Compare Optimistic Concurrency Control (ETag / version columns) vs Pessimistic Locking for collaborative web edits.
reference_answer: Pessimistic row locks hold DB locks across slow human think-time, starving concurrency; Optimistic Concurrency ships an ETag or version integer to the client and enforces UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND version=? rejecting stale saves with 409 Conflict for clean merge UI.

question_text: Explain Service Workers caching strategies (Cache-First, Network-First, Stale-While-Revalidate) and how stale SW upgrades break SPAs.
reference_answer: Cache-First fits hashed immutable JS bundles; Network-First suits critical dynamic HTML/API data. If a newly deployed HTML references new chunk hashes while an active old Service Worker still intercepts fetches serving cached chunks—or updates mid-session—lazy route imports throw ChunkLoadError unless skipWaiting/versioned asset manifests coordinate reloads cleanly.

question_text: How do Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, and Request Smuggling (CL.TE / TE.CL) vulnerabilities arise in multi-tier HTTP proxies?
reference_answer: When a frontend reverse proxy and backend app disagree on Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding parsing on keep-alive HTTP/1.1 connections, attacker bytes bleed into the next user's pipelined request; prevent by speaking clean HTTP/2 upstream or rejecting ambiguous dual headers strictly.

question_text: Design a multi-tenant Rate Limiting and Quota system (sliding window + token bucket) cleanly across distributed API servers.
reference_answer: Implement atomic Redis Lua scripts executing Token Bucket (allowing short human bursts) alongside Sliding-Window counters keyed by tenant/user/IP, returning standard Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers with fail-open degradation circuit breakers if Redis lags.

question_text: Analyze WebAssembly (WASM) vs JavaScript performance trade-offs in browser web applications.
reference_answer: WASM shines on sustained compute-heavy loops (video codecs, audio DSP, local vector math, CAD engines) avoiding JS JIT warmup/GC pauses; however small frequent JS-WASM boundary calls and DOM manipulation incur serialization overhead making plain JS faster for normal UI logic.

question_text: How do you debug Hydration Mismatch errors in Next.js/SSR React apps, and what subtle bugs trigger them?
reference_answer: Hydration fails when server-rendered HTML differs from client first-render JSX—commonly caused by Date.now()/Math.random(), localStorage reads during initial render, invalid nested HTML (like nested paragraph tags), or timezone differences; defer client-only branches cleanly into useEffect or pass deterministic server snapshots.

question_text: Compare Cookie Encryption/HMAC Signing vs Opaque Server Tokens for storing client-side preferences and auth state safely.
reference_answer: Signed cookies remain client-readable yet tamper-proof; encrypted cookies hide payload contents from users/extensions without DB lookups, though still vulnerable to replay before expiry unless backed by server revocation lists like opaque tokens.

question_text: Explain how Head-of-Line blocking behaves across TCP, HTTP/2 streams, and WebSockets when transmitting mixed small UI updates and huge file payloads.
reference_answer: Sending huge files interleaved on one WebSocket frames stalls small control heartbeats behind queued buffers unless frames are chunked small with priority queues; over HTTP/2, priority scheduling interleaves independent streams at the framing layer though single-TCP packet loss still pauses all streams until retransmitted.

question_text: Design a safe Markdown + LaTeX equation rendering pipeline for an educational Copilot UI that prevents Raw HTML block breakage and XSS.
reference_answer: Normalize stored strings stripping unsafe HTML tags at ingestion; render text strictly via CommonMark AST without enabling arbitrary raw HTML or accidental 4-space indented code blocks; render trusted LaTeX solely via KaTeX/MathJax math delimiters with strict macro limits.

question_text: Analyze Clickjacking (UI Redressing) and modern defenses using CSP frame-ancestors vs legacy X-Frame-Options.
reference_answer: Attackers embed invisible victim iframes positioned beneath deceptive buttons to hijack clicks; CSP frame-ancestors 'none' (or exact trusted parent origins) supersedes legacy X-Frame-Options reliably across modern browsers and supports multi-domain framing policies cleanly.

question_text: How do you profile and eliminate excessive database round-trips (N+1 queries) in FastAPI + SQLAlchemy async endpoints?
reference_answer: Enable SQL echo/OTel spans per request to spot repeated child selects inside loops; load relationships eagerly via selectinload() or joinedload(), project only needed columns, and push aggregations/filtering directly into single SQL queries.

question_text: Compare Sticky Sessions vs Stateless Session Stores when running Streamlit/Stateful WebSocket apps behind an AWS ALB.
reference_answer: Streamlit keeps live widget trees and in-memory script threads tied to a single backend container's WebSocket—requiring ALB cookie-based Sticky Sessions plus graceful draining on scale-in, whereas stateless REST/JWT APIs allow pure round-robin horizontal scaling.

question_text: Explain Prototype Pollution attacks in JavaScript/Node.js backends and strict object-merging defenses.
reference_answer: Unsafe recursive merge helpers processing attacker JSON keys like '__proto__' or 'constructor.prototype' mutate Object.prototype globally across the app enabling auth bypass or RCE; defend using Map/Object.create(null), strict schema validation (Zod/AJV), and explicitly rejecting __proto__/constructor keys.

question_text: How does Connection Pooling (SQLAlchemy QueuePool vs PgBouncer transaction pooling) affect prepared statements and latency?
reference_answer: Server-side connection reuse cuts TCP/TLS/fork startup cost; however running PgBouncer in transaction pooling reassigns backend DB connections between transactions, breaking session-level prepared statements unless protocol-level unnamed statements or statement-cache disablement are configured.

question_text: Explain how Browser Memory Caches (BFCache - Back/Forward Cache) work and which anti-patterns disqualify pages from instant back navigation.
reference_answer: BFCache snapshots an entire live page's JS heap and DOM in memory when navigating away for instant zero-network Back button restores; registering legacy unload listeners, keeping open IndexedDB transactions/WebSockets, or Cache-Control: no-store blocks BFCache eligibility.

question_text: Compare Webhook Delivery Reliability designs: signatures, replay timestamp tolerances, asynchronous processing, and dead-letter queues.
reference_answer: Verify HMAC-SHA256 webhook signatures with constant-time comparison and enforce a tight 5-minute timestamp tolerance against replay; respond 200 OK immediately after queuing payload validation asynchronously so slow downstream consumers never trigger sender retry storms, routing permanent failures to a DLQ.

question_text: How do you diagnose and fix Memory Bloat in Python FastAPI workers handling large multi-megabyte file uploads or ML numpy arrays?
reference_answer: Streaming UploadFile chunks directly to disk/S3 via SpooledTemporaryFile avoids loading huge files into Python heap; Python's pymalloc arena fragmentation often retains RSS after big transient dicts/lists, mitigated via bounded worker max-requests recycling, explicit array del/chunking, and jemalloc.

question_text: Analyze Blue-Green vs Canary vs Rolling Deployments for full-stack web apps with backward-incompatible API changes.
reference_answer: Rolling updates briefly mix old frontend assets hitting new backends (causing schema errors unless APIs stay N-1 backward compatible); Blue-Green switches traffic atomically yet needs instant rollback readiness; Canary shifts 1-5% live traffic checking error/latency SLOs before full rollout.

question_text: Explain CORS preflight caching pitfalls when an API serves multiple allowed frontend origins behind a shared CDN.
reference_answer: If a CDN caches an OPTIONS or GET response carrying Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app1.com without including Vary: Origin, a subsequent user from https://app2.com receives the wrong origin header and fails browser CORS cleanly—always set Vary: Origin whenever Origin varies.

question_text: Design a secure Presigned URL Direct-to-Object-Storage (S3/GCS) upload architecture offloading backend API bandwidth cleanly.
reference_answer: Authenticated client requests POST /uploads/init with filename/size/mime; backend validates auth/quotas and returns a short-lived S3 presigned POST/PUT policy pinning exact content-type, max size, and UUID key; browser uploads straight to S3, then S3 event webhook verifies magic-bytes asynchronously before marking DB row ready.

question_text: Compare Server-Driven UI vs Schema-Validated Client Components in multi-platform interview applications.
reference_answer: Server-Driven UI ships layout component trees dynamically from backend endpoints enabling instant experiments without app-store releases, at the cost of strict backward version contracts for old clients; strongly typed client component schemas keep offline caching, complex audio state, and animations far smoother.

question_text: How do Timing Attacks leak authentication secrets (like password reset tokens or OTP hashes), and how do constant-time checks prevent them?
reference_answer: Naive string == exits at the very first mismatched byte, creating microsecond timing deltas observable statistically over network samples to deduce prefix characters; hmac.compare_digest hashes or XOR-accumulates every byte unconditionally regardless of mismatch index.

question_text: Explain Structured Concurrency (asyncio TaskGroup / AnyIO nurseries) vs unguarded asyncio.create_task() in Python web backends.
reference_answer: Bare create_task() risks silent swallowed exceptions, orphaned background tasks outliving request scopes, and dangling DB connections on cancellation; TaskGroup enforces child task lifetimes strictly inside the parent scope, propagating errors and cancelling siblings cleanly together.

question_text: Compare CSS-in-JS runtime libraries vs Zero-Runtime CSS (Tailwind / CSS Modules) on INP and SSR streaming performance.
reference_answer: Runtime CSS-in-JS injects style tags dynamically during JS hydration adding bundle size, runtime style recalculation overhead on interaction (hurting INP), and streaming SSR complexity; zero-runtime Tailwind/CSS Modules compile static stylesheets upfront bypassing runtime style generation cleanly.

question_text: How do you isolate untrusted user code or LaTeX/document converters safely on a web backend without risking container escape?
reference_answer: Never run shell commands with unsanitized strings inside the main API container; isolate converters inside unprivileged rootless ephemeral containers/gVisor/Firecracker sandboxes with seccomp syscall filters, dropped Linux capabilities, strict cgroup CPU/RAM/timeout caps, and no network egress.

question_text: Diagnose why client-side browser storage (localStorage) causes stale state bugs in multi-tab authenticated web sessions.
reference_answer: localStorage is synchronous and global across tabs without native locking; logging out or switching users in Tab B leaves Tab A executing stale cached requests—listen to window 'storage' events across tabs (or BroadcastChannel) to sync auth resets immediately.

question_text: Explain TLS Mutual Authentication (mTLS) vs API Keys for internal backend-to-backend service calls.
reference_answer: Static API keys leak cleanly in logs/configs and prove only bearer possession; mTLS binds identity cryptographically to short-lived X.509 client/server SPIFFE certificates rotated automatically so both caller and callee verify identity at the TLS handshake before HTTP parsing.

question_text: Design a progressive Question Bank search UI & API handling 2,200+ items with URL-synced filters, debounced search, fast SQLite FTS5, and zero layout shift.
reference_answer: Sync filter state (q, topic, round, difficulty, sort, page) cleanly into query params; debounce search inputs 250ms cancelling prior in-flight fetches; index SQLite questions with FTS5 BM25 + composite `(topic, round, difficulty)` indexes returning 15-item slices plus exact facet counts in <10ms; render fixed-height skeleton/cards cleanly preventing CLS.

question_text: Compare Session Fixation vs Session Hijacking attacks and detail complete lifecycle controls defeating both.
reference_answer: Session Fixation pre-plants a known session ID into a victim's browser before login so the attacker shares the newly elevated session; always regenerate/rotate a fresh cryptographically random session token immediately upon authentication, bind Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags, and terminate sessions cleanly on privilege change or logout.

question_text: Analyze why HTTP/2 Connection Coalescing or CDN Misrouting happens when multiple subdomains share a wildcard TLS certificate.
reference_answer: Browsers reuse an existing HTTP/2 TCP connection across distinct hostnames if their DNS IPs and wildcard SAN certificate overlap; if one edge backend fails to check the HTTP Host/:authority header or skips origin validation, requests for subdomain B route silently onto subdomain A unless authoritative status 421 Misdirected Request is returned.

question_text: How do you architect reliable end-to-end automated testing for a FastAPI + Streamlit + LLM web app without flaky LLM network calls?
reference_answer: Split tests cleanly: unit/integration suites mock external LLM/SMTP clients behind deterministic dependency injection testing exact SQL schemas, auth lockouts, HTML sanitization, and FastAPI validation; run Streamlit AppTest / headless browser E2E smoke tests against local seeded test DBs, reserving narrow nightly live-API integration tests separately.

question_text: Explain Circuit Breakers and Bulkheads when a web backend integrates flaky third-party AI APIs (Groq, Whisper, SMTP).
reference_answer: A Bulkhead caps concurrent thread/semaphore pools per external provider so a slow SMTP or Whisper service cannot exhaust threads serving fast local DB endpoints; a Circuit Breaker trips Open after consecutive 5xx/timeouts failing fast or serving cached/rule-based fallbacks while probing half-open periodically.

question_text: Evaluate XSS & HTML Injection defenses in Python/Streamlit UIs: why does st.markdown(..., unsafe_allow_html=True) break and expose apps, and how do you structure safe custom cards?
reference_answer: Passing unescaped user/LLM text into unsafe_allow_html opens stored XSS cleanly, while indented 4-space HTML template lines trigger CommonMark `<pre><code>` code blocks breaking layout; keep HTML strictly unindented for trusted container wrappers only, html-escape any dynamic label text, and render arbitrary question/answer Markdown strictly via safe native components.

question_text: Compare Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR), Dynamic SSR with Edge CDN Stale-While-Revalidate, and Client-Fetched Personalized Shells.
reference_answer: ISR rebuilds static public pages on time/webhook triggers ideal for catalogs; Dynamic SSR with s-maxage + stale-while-revalidate caches public reads at edge PoPs cleanly; authenticated personalized dashboards pair static edge shells or private SSR with fast per-user API hydration keeping personal PII safely uncached.

question_text: Explain WebSocket Backpressure handling when a slow mobile browser cannot consume rapid server events fast enough.
reference_answer: Unbounded server send buffers inflate worker RAM until OOM kill; inspect socket bufferedAmount / asyncio drain high-water marks, coalesce intermediate non-critical status ticks, drop stale metrics, or shed slow consumers gracefully with clear reconnect codes.

question_text: Design an audit-ready RBAC and PII logging policy for a FastAPI educational backend storing student resumes and interview transcripts.
reference_answer: Enforce owner-scoped queries (WHERE user_email = current_user.email) on every document/session route eliminating IDOR flaws; scrub authorization headers, OTPs, emails, and raw resume bodies from structured application logs; encrypt sensitive backups at rest and honor cascade-delete endpoints cleanly.

question_text: Compare GraphQL Persisted Queries vs Dynamic Ad-Hoc Queries regarding security (DoS/depth attacks) and CDN caching.
reference_answer: Arbitrary deep nested GraphQL queries enable cheap O(2^d) CPU/DB DoS attacks and defeat GET CDN caches; Automated/Allowlisted Persisted Queries map fixed query hashes upfront permitting safe GET CDN caching while rejecting unapproved query ASTs, depth extremes, and complexity bombs.

question_text: Analyze how Eventual Consistency after a Write impacts UX ('Read-Your-Own-Writes') behind Read-Replica Databases and how to solve it cleanly.
reference_answer: If a candidate uploads a resume (primary DB) then immediately refreshes Diagnostics (routed to a slightly lagged read replica), the document appears missing; pin the user's session to primary reads for a brief post-write window, pass causal LSN watermarks, or update client cache optimistically from the write response.

question_text: How do Content-Addressable Asset Pipelines (hashed bundle filenames + immutable Cache-Control) interact with HTML entrypoints during deploys?
reference_answer: Static JS/CSS assets include content hashes (app.8f2a9c.js) served with max-age=31536000, immutable so returning browsers load zero network bytes; index.html itself must stay Cache-Control: no-cache (ETag validated) so browsers immediately pick up updated chunk manifests on every release.

question_text: Diagnose a memory leak caused by fast-firing FastAPI Dependency Caching or Singleton LRU caches over user-bound arguments.
reference_answer: Decorating instance methods or user-scoped functions with @functools.lru_cache holds strong references to self and every user/session argument forever preventing garbage collection; bind caches cleanly to bounded TTL stores, pure stateless inputs, or weakrefs.

question_text: Explain Request Coalescing / Singleflight across distributed web tiers and when non-idempotent requests must bypass it.
reference_answer: Singleflight deduplicates simultaneous identical read lookups (e.g., 500 concurrent requests hitting one uncached catalog item) into one origin query sharing its result; mutations (POST/PATCH) and user-private authorized reads must NEVER be coalesced across users to avoid state/PII leaks.

question_text: How do you verify backward and forward compatibility of JSON API contracts across independent frontend and backend release trains?
reference_answer: Make server responses strictly additive (never rename/remove/change field types without versioning), tolerate unknown fields on clients, enforce optional defaults on newly added request inputs, and run automated consumer-driven OpenAPI/Pact contract tests in CI before merge.

question_text: Analyze how Browser Extension script injection and CORS/CSP interplay when hardening sensitive web portals.
reference_answer: Browser extensions run in isolated worlds able to read/alter DOM text bypassing page CSP rules; sensitive portals minimize plaintext secrets in DOM inputs, rely strictly on HttpOnly session cookies inaccessible to JS/content scripts, keep CSP tight against third-party scripts, and require step-up verification for destructive actions.

question_text: Explain CSS Grid implicit vs explicit tracks, minmax(), auto-fit vs auto-fill for responsive card layouts without media queries.
reference_answer: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr)) collapses empty phantom columns expanding cards cleanly across rows, whereas auto-fill preserves empty column tracks waiting at minimum width inside the grid container.

question_text: Compare CSS position values (static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) and what establishes a containing block for absolute children.
reference_answer: relative offsets from normal flow while anchoring non-static positioned children; absolute pulls out of flow relative to nearest positioned ancestor; fixed locks to viewport (unless an ancestor sets transform/filter); sticky toggles between relative and fixed at scroll thresholds.

question_text: Explain Keyboard Focus Management, tabindex semantics (0 vs -1 vs positive), and accessible modal dialog focus trapping.
reference_answer: tabindex='0' adds custom controls into natural DOM tab order; tabindex='-1' enables programmatic .focus() without polluting sequential tabbing; modals trap Tab focus internally, close cleanly on Escape, and restore focus back to the triggering element.

question_text: How do ARIA live regions (aria-live='polite' vs 'assertive') announce dynamic API errors or chat updates to screen readers safely?
reference_answer: Polite waits cleanly until current speech finishes before announcing updates like toast confirmations; assertive interrupts immediately reserved strictly for urgent validation errors or session timeouts.

question_text: Compare JavaScript Map/Set vs plain Object/Array for dynamic string keys, iteration order, and prototype collisions.
reference_answer: Plain objects inherit Object.prototype keys like toString/constructor and coerce keys to strings; Map accepts arbitrary key types, preserves insertion order cleanly, exposes O(1) .size, and safely avoids prototype lookup collisions.

question_text: Explain WeakMap and WeakSet in JavaScript and why they prevent memory leaks when associating metadata with DOM nodes.
reference_answer: Keys in WeakMap/WeakSet must be objects held via weak references; once a DOM element is removed from the page and unreferenced elsewhere, GC collects both the node and its WeakMap metadata automatically.

question_text: Compare Fetch API error handling behavior against Axios when receiving HTTP 404 or 500 responses.
reference_answer: Axios automatically rejects the Promise on non-2xx statuses, whereas native fetch() resolves normally on 404/500 and only rejects on network/abort errors—requiring explicit checks on response.ok before parsing response.json().

question_text: How does AbortController cancel stale fetch requests and add clean request timeouts in modern JavaScript?
reference_answer: Passing controller.signal into fetch() and calling controller.abort() (or using AbortSignal.timeout(ms)) immediately aborts in-flight HTTP sockets and rejects with AbortError, saving bandwidth and preventing race overwrites.

question_text: Explain HTTP Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) and how preload protects the very first insecure http:// request.
reference_answer: Strict-Transport-Security instructs browsers to upgrade all future domain requests to HTTPS internally for max-age; adding domain to the browser HSTS preload list prevents initial plain-HTTP SSL-stripping attacks before any header is ever seen.

question_text: Explain Referrer-Policy headers (strict-origin-when-cross-origin vs no-referrer) and why password-reset URLs need care.
reference_answer: Default Referer headers can leak sensitive URL tokens in query strings when users click outbound external links; using strict-origin-when-cross-origin strips paths/queries cross-origin, while avoiding secret tokens in URLs prevents exposure altogether.

question_text: Compare Form-Encoded (application/x-www-form-urlencoded), Multipart Form Data, and Application JSON request payloads cleanly.
reference_answer: URL-encoded handles simple ASCII key-values from classic forms; multipart/form-data separates binary files (PDF/WAV) alongside text fields via boundary markers cleanly without base64 33% bloat; JSON handles structured nested API DTOs.

question_text: Explain Conditional HTTP Requests (If-Modified-Since vs If-None-Match) and why ETag wins over timestamps.
reference_answer: Last-Modified only has 1-second resolution and drifts across clock skew or rebuilds leaving bytes identical; strong/weak ETag hashes reflect exact content representations reliably yielding 304 Not Modified.

question_text: Compare Strict Validation vs Mass Assignment (Over-Posting) vulnerabilities in Python/FastAPI ORMs.
reference_answer: Passing raw request dictionaries straight into ORM constructors lets attackers supply hidden fields like is_admin=True or role='admin'; explicit Pydantic schemas separating Create/Update input fields from DB models block mass assignment cleanly.

question_text: Explain HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, Retry-After headers, and client-side rate-limit handling.
reference_answer: When quota/rate thresholds trip, backends return 429 with Retry-After seconds/timestamp; clean frontends disable rapid duplicate clicks, display exact remaining cooldown UX instead of cryptic retries, and respect backoff intervals.

question_text: Compare URL Query Encoding (encodeURIComponent vs encodeURI) when passing search queries like 'C++ & Python' to APIs.
reference_answer: encodeURI leaves reserved delimiters (&, =, +, ?) untouched suited only for whole URLs; passing search filters like 'C++ & Python' without encodeURIComponent/URLSearchParams breaks query splitting around '&' and '+' -> spaces.

question_text: How do React useEffect cleanup functions, dependency arrays, and StrictMode double-invocation catch side-effect bugs early?
reference_answer: Missing dependencies read stale closures; failing to return cleanup (clearing timers, unsubscribing sockets, aborting fetches) leaks listeners; React 18+ dev StrictMode intentionally mounts-unmounts-remounts effects exposing uncleaned leaks immediately.

question_text: Compare Controlled vs Uncontrolled form inputs in React/SPA frameworks regarding validation and re-render frequency.
reference_answer: Controlled components tie input value straight to React state enabling instant validation/formatting at keystroke cost; Uncontrolled inputs let the DOM hold state via refs/FormData minimizing re-renders on massive forms.

question_text: Explain why array index should not be used as a React key in dynamic reorderable or filterable question lists.
reference_answer: When items insert, delete, or sort, array indices shift across different questions causing React to mismatch existing stateful DOM nodes (checkboxes, expanded answers, inputs) onto wrong list entries; use stable unique DB IDs instead.

question_text: How do useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo prevent wasted subtree renders—and when does premature memoization backfire?
reference_answer: React.memo skips child renders when props stay shallow-equal, supported by stable useCallback functions and useMemo objects; overusing them on cheap leaf components adds hook comparison memory/CPU overhead worse than clean component composition.

question_text: Compare Prop Drilling, React Context API, and dedicated state stores (Zustand / Redux / TanStack Query) for server vs UI state.
reference_answer: Server cache state belongs in query libraries handling dedup, stale cache, and loading states; Context fits low-frequency theme/auth globals (broad Context updates trigger all consumers); Zustand cleanly isolates granular high-frequency client state.

question_text: Explain Cross-Tab Authentication Sync patterns when a user logs out or refreshes tokens in one browser tab while another stays open.
reference_answer: BroadcastChannel or window 'storage' events broadcast logout/token updates across open same-origin tabs immediately so background tabs purge sensitive user state and avoid submitting orphan mutations.

question_text: Compare IntersectionObserver vs scroll event listeners for lazy-loading images and infinite question feeds.
reference_answer: Scroll listeners fire dozens of times per second on the main thread forcing expensive getBoundingClientRect() layout checks; IntersectionObserver asynchronously invokes callbacks off-thread only when observed elements cross viewport thresholds cleanly.

question_text: Explain Shadow DOM encapsulation in Web Components vs CSS Modules for third-party embedded UI widgets.
reference_answer: CSS Modules mangle class names at build time cleanly within one bundle; Shadow DOM creates a browser-native scoped DOM & style boundary isolating custom widgets (like embedded Streamlit/chat widgets) from outer host stylesheets completely.

question_text: How does FastAPI's Lifespan Context Manager replace deprecated on_event startup/shutdown handlers cleanly?
reference_answer: @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app) initializes DB pools, warm indexes, and HTTPX clients before yield (startup) and tears them down deterministically after yield (shutdown) using clean scoped resources shared safely across tests.

question_text: Explain Custom Exception Handlers and RFC 7807 / RFC 9457 Problem Details JSON formatting in REST backends.
reference_answer: Consistent Problem Details payloads (type, title, status, detail, instance) paired with centralized app.exception_handler wrappers prevent leaking raw tracebacks while giving frontend clients predictable actionable error objects.

question_text: Compare Database Migrations (Alembic / Flyway) against auto-creating tables via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in app startup.
reference_answer: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cannot add columns, modify constraints, rename fields, or backfill existing tables cleanly; versioned migrations apply deterministic incremental forward/rollback changes under locks cleanly across dev/staging/prod.

question_text: How do you protect FastAPI / REST endpoints against ReDoS and oversized deeply nested JSON payloads?
reference_answer: Enforce reverse-proxy client_max_body_size caps, validate max string length / nesting limits on Pydantic fields explicitly, prefer simple linear string operations over complex nested-quantifier regexes, and configure Uvicorn request limits.

question_text: Explain Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerabilities in GET/DELETE APIs and enforce systematic ownership checks.
reference_answer: Exposing sequential or predictable IDs (/api/v1/sessions/42) without filtering WHERE user_email = current_user.email allows logged-in users to read or delete peers' private interview sessions; enforce tenant/owner filters strictly on every query.

question_text: Compare Soft Deletes (deleted_at timestamp) vs Hard Deletes in web databases when compliance (GDPR erasure) applies.
reference_answer: Soft deletes preserve foreign keys, analytics history, and accidental-delete undo easily via partial indexes, yet fail strict legal data-erasure obligations; GDPR flows require hard PII deletion/anonymization paired cleanly with aggregate stats.

question_text: Explain SQLite FTS5 Full-Text Search integration inside a web API compared to SQL LIKE '%keyword%' scans.
reference_answer: Leading-wildcard LIKE '%keyword%' bypasses B-Tree indexes causing slow full table scans without word stemming or relevance ranking; SQLite FTS5 inverted indexes tokenize words, rank matches with BM25 scores, and handle prefix/phrase search cleanly.

question_text: How do you cleanly serve Large Audio/Video files over HTTP supporting Seeking/Scrubbing without downloading entire files?
reference_answer: Support HTTP Range requests (Accept-Ranges: bytes, parsing Range: bytes=start-end headers) and stream partial chunks cleanly returning status 206 Partial Content with accurate Content-Range headers.

question_text: Compare Reverse Proxy TLS Termination vs End-to-End TLS encryption inside private cloud VPC networks.
reference_answer: Proxy TLS termination simplifies certificate management and unlocks HTTP header inspection/caching cleanly; high-security zero-trust networks extend mTLS/TLS all the way inside backend pods protecting east-west traffic against lateral sniffing.

question_text: Explain Prefetching vs Prerendering (Speculation Rules API) vs Preloading in modern browsers.
reference_answer: Preload fetches critical resources needed for the *current* navigation urgently; Prefetch hints low-priority assets likely needed on the *next* route; Speculation Rules can prerender likely next navigations into hidden background tabs cleanly for instant transitions.

question_text: Compare Responsive Image techniques (srcset, sizes, picture element, WebP/AVIF, explicit width/height) cleanly.
reference_answer: Always reserve intrinsic aspect ratio via width/height attributes preventing CLS layout jump; wrap AVIF/WebP fallbacks inside picture elements; supply resolution/width descriptors via srcset + sizes so mobile screens never download 4K desktop hero images.

question_text: Explain Font Loading strategies (font-display: swap vs optional, WOFF2 subsetting, preconnect) eliminating invisible text FOIT.
reference_answer: Standard web fonts hide text up to 3s causing Flash of Invisible Text; WOFF2 compresses glyphs smallest, font-display: swap renders system fallback instantly before swapping, and optional eliminates late layout shift cleanly on slow networks.

question_text: How do CSS Custom Properties (Variables) differ from Sass/SCSS variables cleanly at runtime?
reference_answer: Sass variables compile statically away at build time and cannot respond dynamically to DOM structure or media queries; CSS custom properties cascade live through the DOM, update dynamically via JS/themes/dark mode cleanly, and inspect in DevTools.

question_text: Explain Container Queries (@container) in modern CSS and why they solve reusable component layout pain compared to viewport @media.
reference_answer: Components inside sidebars vs wide grids care about their own wrapper width rather than total browser window width; container-type: inline-size lets cards adapt cleanly between stacked vs horizontal layouts anywhere they are mounted.

question_text: Compare HTTP Keep-Alive persistent connections vs Connection: close on API server throughput and ephemeral port exhaustion.
reference_answer: Opening new TCP+TLS connections per REST call wastes RTT latency and can exhaust TIME_WAIT ephemeral sockets under high RPS; persistent HTTP Keep-Alive pools reuse warm sockets across bursts when keepalive timeouts exceed proxy timeouts.

question_text: Explain how Browser DevTools Network Waterfall bars (DNS, Initial Connection, SSL, TTFB, Content Download) isolate backend vs frontend slowness.
reference_answer: Slow Waiting/TTFB points directly to backend DB/API compute or cold starts; high Queueing/Stalled hints HTTP/1.1 connection limits; long Content Download flags uncompressed bulky JSON/assets or slow client pipes.

question_text: Compare JSON Schema Validation on both Client Forms and Server APIs—why isn't frontend validation alone sufficient?
reference_answer: Frontend checks provide instant user UX feedback saving round trips, yet attackers bypass UI JavaScript trivially via curl/Postman/DevTools; backend validation remains the sole authoritative security & data-integrity gate.

question_text: How do Feature Flags (Trunk-Based Development) decouple code Deployment from User Feature Release cleanly?
reference_answer: Incomplete features deploy safely dark behind server/client config flags evaluated cleanly at runtime, enabling incremental user canary percentages, rapid zero-deploy kill switches on bugs, and clean A/B rollouts without long-lived merge conflicts.

question_text: Explain OpenAPI / Swagger automatic schema generation pitfalls when FastAPI routes return untyped dicts instead of Pydantic models.
reference_answer: Returning raw dicts skips response serialization validation, loses automated OpenAPI/TypeScript SDK client types, and risks accidentally leaking unstripped internal keys (password hashes/debug flags) into API responses.

question_text: Compare Long-Lived API Keys vs Short-Lived Scoped Tokens for authenticating service-to-service integrations.
reference_answer: Static API keys require manual rotation and grant permanent broad access upon leakage; short-lived OAuth2 Client Credentials or workload-identity JWTs bound cleanly to minimal scopes automatically expire limiting breach windows.

question_text: Explain Exponential Backoff, Circuit Breaking, and Timeout Budgets when a web API calls downstream LLM endpoints cleanly.
reference_answer: Never leave external LLM HTTP calls without strict connect + read timeouts; pass bounded deadlines across retries cleanly so cascading retry storms never tie up worker pools when an upstream model endpoint stalls.

question_text: Compare Cursor Pagination vs Keyset Pagination over multi-column sorts like (score DESC, id ASC).
reference_answer: Offset pagination shifts rows on inserts; pure timestamp cursors skip duplicate timestamps; deterministic keyset tuples WHERE (score, id) < (last_score, last_id) encoded opaquely in base64 cursors guarantee O(1) index seeks without missing ties.

question_text: How do Cross-Origin Resource Policy (CORP) and Timing-Allow-Origin headers protect user privacy across embedded cross-origin media?
reference_answer: CORP blocks malicious third-party sites from embedding sensitive private assets via script/img elements preventing Spectre side-channel reads, while Timing-Allow-Origin selectively exposes high-res PerformanceResourceTiming breakdown across authorized CDNs.

question_text: Explain how Browser Form Autofill, Autocomplete attributes, and Password Managers interact securely with login/OTP pages.
reference_answer: Proper type='email', autocomplete='email', and autocomplete='one-time-code' trigger mobile/browser OTP autofill smoothly while disabling autocomplete cleanly on sensitive ephemeral tokens prevents accidental caching.

question_text: Compare Server-Generated CSV/PDF Export streaming vs building large export files completely in backend RAM before returning.
reference_answer: Building 500k-row CSVs in memory triggers worker OOM spikes and proxy TTFB timeouts; Python StreamingResponse yielding rows lazily from a DB cursor flushes bytes progressively in constant O(1) memory.

question_text: Explain how CSS prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme media queries support inclusive adaptive frontend UIs.
reference_answer: prefers-reduced-motion disables jarring parallax/sliding animations cleanly for vestibular-sensitive users, while prefers-color-scheme aligns initial theme tokens smoothly with OS dark/light defaults without white flash flicker.
