question_text: Compare URL Hash routing (#/section) vs HTML5 History API routing (/section) in Single-Page Applications.
reference_answer: Hash routes never hit the backend server requiring zero proxy config yet hurt SEO and clean links; History API pushState produces clean paths requiring backend fallback rewrite serving index.html on deep refreshes (while preserving API 404s cleanly).

question_text: How do you isolate Stateful Per-User Caches in Python Web Apps so Candidate A never receives Candidate B's cached dashboard data?
reference_answer: Include explicit authenticated user/tenant ID inside every cache key, avoid bare @lru_cache on global helpers accessing request globals, enforce strict HTTP Vary / Cache-Control: private, no-store on personalized JSON routes, and validate keys in tests.

question_text: Explain Browser Storage Quotas, Eviction Policies, and when IndexedDB beats localStorage for offline web data.
reference_answer: localStorage caps synchronously at ~5-10MB blocking the main UI thread on large JSON parsing; IndexedDB operates asynchronously supporting structured binary blobs (audio recordings, embeddings, thousands of items) across hundreds of megabytes cleanly.

question_text: Compare Event-Driven Microservice Webhooks vs Polling Status Endpoints for long-running PDF ingestion or Audio scoring jobs.
reference_answer: HTTP POST kicks off background jobs quickly returning 202 Accepted + job_id; client polling with jitter/SSE works seamlessly for browsers behind NAT, while signed async webhooks fit backend-to-backend integrations cleanly.

question_text: How does FastAPI Handle Uploaded File Validation cleanly (MIME inspection via python-magic/header bytes + extension allowlist + size streaming)?
reference_answer: Read an initial header slice inspecting exact magic signatures (%PDF-, RIFF/WAVE, OggS) plus strict max byte counters cleanly across async file chunks, rejecting spoofed .exe files renamed to .pdf before passing files to downstream parsers.

question_text: Explain JavaScript Strict Mode ('use strict') and subtle silent failure modes it converts into explicit exceptions cleanly.
reference_answer: Strict mode throws TypeError instead of silently creating accidental global variables on mistyped assignments, forbids duplicate parameter names, throws on writing non-writable properties, and leaves unbound 'this' cleanly undefined instead of global window.

question_text: Compare HTTP GET Query Caching vs GraphQL/POST Search Caching trade-offs when designing Question Bank filter endpoints.
reference_answer: Encoding search filters cleanly in GET query params (?topic=python&difficulty=medium&page=1) unlocks shareable deep-links, browser Back-button history, and effortless Nginx/CDN edge caching cleanly—unlike opaque POST payloads.

question_text: How do Dependency Lockfiles (package-lock.json / poetry.lock / requirements hashes) protect web applications against supply-chain regressions?
reference_answer: Loose semver pins (^1.4.0) silently pull unreviewed minor/patch releases in CI builds; lockfiles pin exact transitive versions + cryptographic hashes ensuring reproducible builds and preventing sneaky dependency hijacks or breaking patches.

question_text: Explain Structured JSON Error Boundaries in React vs try/catch blocks—what errors do React Error Boundaries NOT catch?
reference_answer: Error Boundaries catch synchronous render, lifecycle, and constructor crashes cleanly showing fallback UI instead of white screens, yet do NOT catch async Promises, event handler throws, or SSR errors—requiring explicit event try/catch and async query error states.

question_text: Compare Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) signals in web backends: CPU utilization vs Request Queue Depth / P95 Latency.
reference_answer: I/O-bound FastAPI workers waiting on LLM APIs or DB locks can hit latency cliffs at only 25% CPU; scaling on active concurrent request queue depth, worker loop lag, or P95 response latency triggers scale-out cleanly before timeouts cascade.

question_text: Explain Clean Session State Lifecycle Design in Streamlit multi-page / multi-tab applications to avoid state leakage between logout/login.
reference_answer: Prefix domain keys consistently (mcq_, audio_, auth_), explicitly clear user-scoped domain keys on logout or user switch, separate server API URL defaults cleanly from candidate session artifacts, and derive active navigation cleanly from verified auth status.

question_text: Compare Synchronous Database Drivers vs Async Drivers (sqlite3/psycopg2 vs aiosqlite/asyncpg) in ASGI FastAPI applications.
reference_answer: Blocking calls inside async def freeze the entire event loop halting unrelated concurrent users; true async drivers yield control cleanly on socket waits—or synchronous drivers must stay isolated inside sync def endpoints delegated to AnyIO worker threads.
